stem:
Yusuf compares how fast equal amounts of water dry. He can use a shallow wide plate or a narrow-necked bottle, and he can change temperature and how humid the air is.

Which claims about evaporation are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: With the same amount, temperature, and humidity, water in the shallow wide plate evaporates faster than water in the narrow-necked bottle.
The wide plate always finishes first, even if it holds much more water than the bottle.
With temperature and exposed area equal, water evaporates faster in dry air than in humid air.
Water near room temperature cannot evaporate at all until it boils.

teacher.key_rationale: Larger exposed surface and drier air speed evaporation when other factors match. Amount must be controlled; boiling is not required for evaporation at room temperature.
